source.title: Kernel Renormalization in Bayesian Deep Neural Networks: the Equivalent Wishart Ansatz in the Proportional Regime
source.authors: P. Baglioni; Christian Keup; Vincenzo Zimbardo; Rosalba Pacelli; A. Vezzani; R. Burioni; P. Rotondo

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and appendices; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures posterior training and test error in finite-width Bayesian networks and compares those results with infinite-width predictions. Its sampling method and questions differ from the claim versions, and it does not test their specified interventions or conditions.
record.gate_note: The study reports training and generalization errors for Bayesian posterior samples and describes how depth, sample-to-width ratio, activation, dataset, and parametrization affect them. It does not test random-label memorization, the stated width sweep for one-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs, FC-versus-CNN generalization, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Several comparisons are reported only in figures; exact values are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study tests its Equivalent Wishart Ansatz against Bayesian posterior sampling, not any V1–V8 claim. Width sweeps measure posterior squared error without establishing a zero-training-error threshold or post-interpolation classification performance. CNN and MLP experiments do not provide a controlled architectural comparison. Keskar et al. and Jiang et al. are cited as background on algorithmic bias; their findings are neither tested nor used as a tool.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. EWA approximately predicts Bayesian finite-width learning curves across the tested architectures and datasets, especially at moderate load. The authors distinguish gradual approximation errors on Gaussian data from abrupt metastable transitions on CIFAR-10 at high depth and load. They attribute the tested µP improvement mainly to reduced predictor variance and caution that apparently stable sampling histories can conceal long equilibration times.
record.recipe_differences: Bayesian posterior inference and MCMC sampling with Gaussian weight priors and squared-error regression, rather than the claim versions' standard training recipes and interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with depth, sample-to-width ratio α, activation, dataset, parametrization and temperature; the metastable transition depends on the sampling phase at large depth and load.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-width Bayesian MLP posterior errors depart from infinite-width predictions. EWA generally tracks them, with gradual deviations at high load and depth on Gaussian teacher data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Bayesian MLP regression, finite-width effects depend on depth and sample-to-width ratio and can be captured approximately by scalar kernel renormalization.

fits_no_version.finding: At α = 2.5 and T = 0.01 in the tested CIFAR-10 ReLU task, posterior sampling shows abrupt training and test loss reductions beginning at L = 6; transient averages remain close to EWA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep Bayesian ReLU networks can exhibit long-lived transient states followed by abrupt improvements in posterior training and test error.

fits_no_version.finding: For the tested shallow Bayesian Erf CNNs, EWA tracks losses across channel counts and approaches NNGP predictions when channel count greatly exceeds sample count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local kernel renormalization can approximately predict finite-channel Bayesian CNN regression errors.

fits_no_version.finding: In the tested four-hidden-layer CIFAR-10 ReLU MLPs, µP with scaled temperature improves posterior generalization primarily through lower predictor variance while bias remains similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this Bayesian proportional-width setting, µP can improve generalization over standard parametrization mainly by suppressing posterior predictor variance.

record.code_released: https://github.com/rpacelli/deepbays (2026-05-28); the paper says full analysis code and numerical results will be provided with the published version.
record.problems: The Equivalent Wishart Ansatz is approximate. The authors report systematic deviations at large depth and load, including an abrupt transition whose sampling requires long runs. They caution that apparently stable MCMC histories may conceal long timescales; one µP example is explicitly poorly converged. Many plotted numerical values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Several supplementary figure-only comparisons are not separately extracted because they repeat the reported dataset/activation/depth learning-curve comparisons without additional textual outcomes.

untested.parts: Paired natural-label and fixed-random-label fitting and held-out classification accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error in converged, unregularized one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparisons, local connectivity, sparse learned connections and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes from longer training or adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data and excessive-dropout regimes, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking relative to norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples compared with equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a version's effect; this does not deny the reported Bayesian results. Appendix F allows finite width to improve or worsen generalization depending on task–kernel overlap, but does not test V2's post-interpolation width claim. Adam in Appendix E optimizes the theoretical effective action and supplies no V4 evidence. No omitted result bearing on V1–V8 was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels in the specified architectures and recipes.
The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP width sweeps on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, including behavior past the zero-training-error threshold.
A controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks, local connectivity, and learned sparse connections.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons and the stated tuning, weight-decay, and switching conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and the stated recipe adaptations.
Dropout intervention comparisons, training-set-size regimes, and dropout or weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining comparisons against random removals.

conditions.value: abrupt drops reported at L = 6; no drops up to L = 5

rows.baseline: transient phase and smooth EWA and large-width predictions; exact values not stated
rows.value: At L = 6, both losses exhibit sudden drops in equilibrium samples; increasing N and P at fixed α makes the drop more pronounced. Transient averages continue the smooth trend and agree with EWA. Exact values are figure only.

rows.note: The result depends on whether the sample is from the transient or equilibrium phase; multiple samplers were used.

rows.baseline: large-width predictions; exact values not stated
rows.value: At large but finite A1 ∼ P, simulations are described as tracked by EWA; EWA approaches large-width predictions for A1 ≫ P. Exact values are figure only.

rows.value: SP and µP generalization errors differ substantially; the paper says the difference is mostly driven by reduced predictor variance in µP, while bias remains similar. Exact values are figure only.

rows.baseline: SP results and large-width predictions; exact values not stated
rows.value: The paper says µP improves generalization over SP mostly through reduced predictor variance, with similar bias; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: The N = 2500 run is described as poorly converged; other point-specific uncertainty values are not stated in text.
rows.locator: Sec. VI F, Fig. 8 and Fig. S7
